entries.subject: DAMIT 5924: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-5924.txt. Model 5924, version 2021-11-12, pole (121°, -27°), period 9.29759 h match the retained metadata. The archive diameter field is 93 ±3 km; its applicability to our scale is a separate calibration decision. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021)
entries.finding: [Vernazza et al. (2021)](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/references/view/660) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI thermal diameter as an alternative scale
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — retained for comparison; the selected archive model has a physical size calibration. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 87.47 ± 1.13 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 63 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.
entries.revisitWhen: A source-specific comparison with the selected shape and physical calibration justifies changing the adopted scale.

entries.subject: Resolved-model publication supporting DAMIT 5924
entries.finding: The live DAMIT model-to-reference export binds selected model 5924 to VLT/SPHERE imaging survey of the largest main-belt asteroids: Final results and synthesis (2021). That publication supports the selected reconstruction. The imported entry conflated three surveys; listing them together did not establish three usable models or a registered reflectance mosaic.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: Included 2026-09-18 as the SPHERE photograph lens: 25 camera-1 deconvolved frames, 2018-09-28 and 2018-09-29, cast onto the ADAM mesh with cameras computed from the release rotation record, JPL Horizons and each frame’s header. Its registration is the published comparison recorded in zimpol-published-comparison. Earlier finding, kept: The release supplies no registered surface imagery; the grid marks that gap.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: Alternative archive solutions: model 140, pole ['120', '-15'], [Model 140](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/140) The live DAMIT export lists these other models for this target: 140: pole (120°, -15°), 9.29759 h, version 2011-03-28, archive diameter 90 km. These are archive alternatives, not necessarily newly released models or preferred replacements. Comparing their source methods and any pole-specific calibration remains necessary before changing the selected mesh.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Decided 2026-09-18 by the published comparison instead: the lens is prepared from 25 camera-1 frames on the ADAM mesh with the rotation record read latitude-first, and ships on zimpol-published-comparison; the registration stage’s numbers are in the README. Earlier result, kept: Measured with the cross-frame registration test on 5 deconvolved ZIMPOL frames (camera 1), each held against a reference built from the body's frames more than an hour away, cast through the ADAM reconstruction with the survey's rotation record read latitude-first. Disc interior 132 pixels (median); peak correlation 0.20 (median) against a mirror margin of 0.54; 0 of 5 frames decisive by the stated rule (peak at least 0.15 and margin at least 1.5), of which 0 peak within 5 degrees of the model. The frames carry no markings the test can register, so nothing in them confirms or refutes the rotation record's phase, pole or handedness; the silhouette gate that qualified Kleopatra cannot judge a body this round either. The lens stands on the silhouette registration recorded in the entry above and on the route proven against the Dawn mosaic on Vesta; this test adds no independent check for this body. Removed on 2026-09-16: a lens ships only when every registration measurement that reaches a verdict places it within three degrees, and this one measured outline systematic 1.93° against relief −8.00°.

entries.subject: Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.28 as the registration of the SPHERE photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured with tools/objects/sphere-survey/setup.mts against Vernazza et al. (2021) Figure B.28, the survey’s comparison of these frames with its models. Outline overlap with the paper’s ADAM panels 0.922 to 0.935 at our phase, against 0.928 to 0.940 for our own outline drawn at the paper’s pixel scale; over a full turn in 10° steps it peaks at our phase in 5 of 6 columns, one step from it in 1. With the paper’s photographs 0.917 to 0.935. Turned in the image, our outline best overlaps the paper’s photographs at -2.0 to 0.5° and its model panels at -6.0 to -1.5°. The spin axis we project lies at 3.5° on the sky against 1.4 to 1.6° for the figure’s arrows. Native outline residual 0.923 px mean over 25 frames at our phase; the sweep’s lowest is 0.921 px at -2°. The figure’s column labels were read from its pixels, and each names a frame’s exposure start to the second. The release rotation record reads latitude-first, 0.14° from the published pole.
